name: Pong
desc: Echoes back the exact client timestamp from C01PacketPing. The client calculates round-trip latency from the difference.

fields.name: clientTime
fields.desc: The exact same timestamp the client sent in C01PacketPing

encoding: Echoed back from C01PacketPing — same System.currentTimeMillis() value
notes: The final packet in the STATUS handshake. After receiving this, OldServerPinger closes the connection and stores the computed latency (pingToServer = currentTime - echoedTime).

writeup.p: The final packet of the STATUS handshake. NetHandlerStatusServer.processPing answers C01PacketPing with `new S01PacketPong(packetIn.getClientTime())`, echoing the client's timestamp untouched. OldServerPinger's anonymous handler computes the server-list latency as `pingToServer = Minecraft.getSystemTime() - echoedTime` and closes the channel with a "Finished" ChatComponentText. The packet carries no other data, so the entire exploit surface is the timing relation between send and echo.

The handler is the anonymous INetHandlerStatusClient that OldServerPinger installs per destination. handleServerInfo stores the response and sends C01PacketPing; handlePong then measures the round trip and closes. RealmsServerStatusPinger mirrors the same two-handler shape for the Realms list. Server side, processPing is stateless: any C01PacketPing in STATUS state gets its timestamp echoed verbatim, with no correlation or deduplication.

The corpus has exactly one non-vanilla reference: Rise 5.99 StaffAlert imports S01PacketPong at line 22, and the import is unused (the module's logic only touches S02PacketChat and the Hypixel API). Every other hit across the 8 clients is vanilla. The practical conclusion is that no module in the corpus touches STATUS ping at all: server-list latency display stays fully vanilla, and the PingSpoof-style modules in these clients all operate on the PLAY-state keepalive (S00PacketKeepAlive/C00PacketKeepAlive) instead.

Delaying or dropping S01PacketPong would only corrupt the local server list entry (frozen or stale ping), with no server-visible effect and no anti-cheat consequence; none of the 8 clients bothers. The server-side surface is the echo itself: processPing is unauthenticated and unthrottled, so a proxy or plugin that wants to fingerprint clients can measure ping intervals, and a flood of C01PacketPing generates an equal flood of S01 replies. For clients, the packet is a dead end.

implementation.overview: The STATUS latency echo. Pure vanilla in 7 of 8 clients; the only module hit is an unused S01PacketPong import in Rise 5.99 StaffAlert. Ping spoofing in these clients targets the PLAY-state keepalive, not the server list.
implementation.server_handling: NetHandlerStatusServer.processPing echoes the clientTime long verbatim via S01PacketPong. No validation, no rate limit, no connection state tracking: the handler is a pure reflector. The client closes the connection immediately after the echo, so the server never sees a follow-up packet in the STATUS state.
implementation.protocol_notes: Wire layout: a single long (8 bytes), the client's System.currentTimeMillis() captured at C01PacketPing send time. The client computes latency locally as now minus echoed value; clock skew is irrelevant because both timestamps are client-side. STATUS state runs before encryption, so the timestamp is readable by any on-path observer, which is how proxies estimate client-server distance.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: None. STATUS ping is outside play state and no anti-cheat samples it. The measurement only feeds the server-list GUI. A client faking its list ping would fool nobody but its own user, which is presumably why the 8 clients never implemented it.

modules.name: StaffAlert
modules.purpose: Hypixel staff-ban tracker. Its reference to this packet is an import only; the module does not use S01PacketPong.
modules.how_it_works: The corpus hit is line 22, `import net.minecraft.network.status.server.S01PacketPong;`. The module's actual logic listens for S02PacketChat (captures the Hypixel API key from chat), sends /api new until the key is set, then polls api.hypixel.net/punishmentstats on a timer thread and notifies on staff-ban deltas. The S01PacketPong, S02PacketLoginSuccess, C00Handshake and S40PacketDisconnect imports are all dead.
modules.vanilla_hook: None for this packet; the module hooks PacketReceiveEvent for S02PacketChat and UpdateEvent for the API polling.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Irrelevant here: the import is never exercised. The dead import is likely a leftover from an earlier design that detected staff via status pings.
modules.variations: No other client has any module reference to S01PacketPong; Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy, Tenacity and both Rise 6.x builds are vanilla-only for this packet.

implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients ship the stock OldServerPinger/RealmsServerStatusPinger/NetHandlerStatusServer. Rise 5.99 alone adds the dead import in StaffAlert; Rise 6.x and Tenacity rename handler params to final but keep behavior identical.

anticheat.overview: The STATUS pong has an empty corpus: zero of the 50 anticheats reference S01PacketPong or PacketStatusOutPong. The echo runs before encryption and world state, carries a single client timestamp, and feeds only the server-list latency display, so there is nothing for a server-side anticheat to measure or flag. Ping spoofing that anticheats do care about targets the play-state keepalive, not this packet.
